task:
SPLIT THE "FINDER DERIVED-DATA TESTS (POSTGRESQL 18)" CI LANE INTO THREE SHARDS BALANCED BY MEASURED RUN TIME, SPLITTING THE ONE DOMINANT MODULE AT TEST LEVEL. CI/TOOLING ONLY. CHANGE EXACTLY THESE PATHS AND NOTHING ELSE: .github/workflows/ci.yml (job `finder-derived-data` only), NEW scripts/ci/finder_derived_data_shards.py, NEW scripts/ci/finder_derived_data_weights.json, NEW scripts/ci/finder_derived_data_weights.py, tests/test_ci_finder_derived_data_lane.py, NEW tests/test_ci_finder_derived_data_shards.py, docs/development/test-environment.md (one job-name mention) and CHANGES.md. DO NOT CHANGE ANY OTHER TEST MODULE, tests/conftest.py, ANY OTHER WORKFLOW OR JOB, OR ANY APPLICATION, OPERATOR, SQL OR DEPLOY FILE.

WHY (measured 2026-10-31): the lane balances modules by file size (`wc -c`) across 2 shards. On PR #936 (head 47b549ea) shard 1/2 ran 488 tests in 2,132 s (35:32) and shard 2/2 ran 376 tests in 918 s (15:18), against a 45-minute pytest bound per shard; on PR #938 the two jobs took 27.3 and 15.7 minutes. Every other CI job takes 5 minutes or less, so this lane is the critical path of every PR. A local PostgreSQL 18 run of all 40 discovered modules (864 passed in 3,630.6 s) shows why file size cannot fix it: tests/test_v3_governed_derived_purge.py alone takes 2,079.6 s (215 tests, every test between 1.8 and 16.1 s, median 10.5 s) of 3,608.7 s, so no split that keeps modules whole can balance three shards. The biggest single test in the lane takes 18.9 s.

CURRENT CODE: .github/workflows/ci.yml job `finder-derived-data`: matrix `shard: [1, 2]`, step "Run every validation-fixture-backed Finder test module". Module discovery is the `grep -lE 'RATINGS_V4_VALIDATION_DATABASE_URL|ratings_v4_pg_fixture|canonical_database' tests/test_*.py | grep -v '^tests/test_ratings_v4' | sort` pipeline; keep it byte-for-byte (tests/test_ci_finder_derived_data_lane.py parses it). Keep the step NAME exactly (tests/test_db_isolation_guardrails.py looks it up). tests/conftest.py has a `pytest_collection_modifyitems` that only adds `integration` marks and a tryfirst `pytest_runtest_logreport` for GitHub annotations; neither reorders or deselects. The job is not a required status check, so renaming it is safe.

DESIGN: every shard passes ALL discovered modules to pytest; a small pytest plugin, loaded with `-p`, computes the same plan on every shard from the collected node ids and deselects everything that is not this shard's. Because every shard collects the identical set and computes the identical plan, the shards together run each test exactly once.

1. NEW scripts/ci/finder_derived_data_shards.py (CPython 3.14; standard library and pytest only; must not import anything from apps/ or tests/):
   a) Constants WEIGHTS_SCHEMA = "finder-derived-data-weights/v1", DURATIONS_SCHEMA = "finder-derived-data-durations/v1", MAX_SHARDS = 8.
   b) `load_weights(path) -> dict[str, float]`: the file must be a JSON object with exactly the keys "measured" (non-empty string), "schema" (== WEIGHTS_SCHEMA) and "seconds" (object). Every seconds key must match `^tests/test_[A-Za-z0-9_]+\.py$` and every value must be a finite number greater than 0 (bool is not a number). Raise ValueError with a one-line message on a missing or unreadable file, invalid JSON, or any violation.
   c) A frozen dataclass `ShardPlan` with `shards: int`, `assignment: dict[str, int]` (node id -> shard number 1..shards), `totals: tuple[float, ...]` (predicted seconds per shard) and `split_modules: tuple[str, ...]` (sorted).
   d) `plan(nodeids: Sequence[str], weights: Mapping[str, float], shards: int, size_of: Callable[[str], int]) -> ShardPlan`:
      - the module of a node id is the text before its first "::" (a node id without "::" is its own module);
      - module weight = weights[module] when listed; otherwise size_of(module) * rate, where rate = (sum of weights of the listed modules present in nodeids) / (sum of size_of over those modules); if no listed module is present, every module weight is size_of(module). Weights entries for modules not present are ignored (a renamed or removed module must never fail CI);
      - total = sum of module weights. A module is SPLIT when its weight > total / (2 * shards), i.e. more than half of one shard's even share: each of its node ids becomes its own unit weighing (module weight / number of its node ids). Every other module is ONE unit holding all its node ids (so module- and class-scoped fixtures still run once per module);
      - longest-processing-time greedy: sort units by weight descending, then by key ascending (the module path for a whole-module unit, the node id for a split unit); give each unit to the shard with the smallest running total, ties to the lowest shard number;
      - raise ValueError (one line) when shards is outside 1..MAX_SHARDS, nodeids is empty or contains a duplicate, or any shard receives no unit.
   e) pytest hooks:
      - `pytest_addoption`: an option group with `--finder-shard` (int), `--finder-shards` (int), `--finder-weights` (path) and `--finder-durations-out` (path).
      - `pytest_configure`: if none of shard/shards/weights is given the plugin does nothing (apart from durations, below). If only some are given, or the shard number is outside 1..shards, or shards is outside 1..MAX_SHARDS, raise pytest.UsageError with a one-line message. Load and validate the weights file here too (load_weights errors become pytest.UsageError), so a bad file fails before collection.
      - `pytest_collection_modifyitems` with `@pytest.hookimpl(trylast=True)`: compute plan(...) over the node ids of `items` (size_of = byte size of `config.rootpath / module`), turning a ValueError into pytest.UsageError. Keep this shard's items IN THEIR ORIGINAL ORDER, report the rest through `config.hook.pytest_deselected(items=...)` and assign `items[:] = kept`. Then write the plan through the terminal reporter (`config.pluginmanager.get_plugin("terminalreporter")`, skipped if None) so it shows under `-q`, in this form (numbers illustrative):
        `finder-derived-data shard 2/3: 300 of 864 tests, predicted 1203.4 s (shard totals 1203.9 / 1203.4 / 1201.5 s)` then one line per whole module of this shard, `  whole: tests/test_x.py`, then one line per split module, `  split: tests/test_y.py (72 of 215 tests)`.
      - durations: when `--finder-durations-out` is given (with or without sharding), sum `report.duration` of every phase per `report.nodeid` in `pytest_runtest_logreport`, and in `pytest_sessionfinish` write `{"exitstatus": <int>, "schema": DURATIONS_SCHEMA, "seconds": {nodeid: seconds rounded to 0.001}, "shard": <int or null>, "shards": <int or null>}` with sorted keys, 2-space indent and a trailing newline, creating parent directories.

2. NEW scripts/ci/finder_derived_data_weights.json, in the exact format the refresh tool writes (sorted keys, 2-space indent, trailing newline): "schema" = WEIGHTS_SCHEMA; "measured" = "2026-10-31: one local PostgreSQL 18 run of all 40 discovered modules, 864 passed in 3,630.6 s; refresh with scripts/ci/finder_derived_data_weights.py from the lane's durations artifacts"; "seconds" = EXACTLY the 40 values under MEASURED SECONDS below.

3. NEW scripts/ci/finder_derived_data_weights.py (refresh tool; standard library plus importing the plugin module from its own directory for the constants and the weights format): `python scripts/ci/finder_derived_data_weights.py --measured TEXT DURATIONS.json [DURATIONS.json ...]` prints the weights JSON of step 2 to stdout: per module (node id text before the first "::") the sum of its node ids' seconds rounded to 0.1, with a rounded value of 0.0 written as 0.1. Exit 2 with a one-line stderr message when: --measured is missing or empty; a file is unreadable, not JSON or not DURATIONS_SCHEMA; a file's exitstatus is not 0; shard/shards are missing or not integers; the files do not all have the same shards K or their shard numbers are not exactly 1..K once each; a node id appears in more than one file (two shards ran the same test); or there are no node ids at all.

4. .github/workflows/ci.yml, job `finder-derived-data` only:
   - matrix `shard: [1, 2, 3]`; job name `Finder derived-data tests (PostgreSQL 18, shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/3)`; keep `fail-fast: false`, `timeout-minutes: 60`, the services, the checkout/setup/install/attest steps and every env value unchanged EXCEPT the run step's PYTHONPATH, which becomes `${{ github.workspace }}/apps/api/src:${{ github.workspace }}/scripts/ci`.
   - run step: keep `set -euo pipefail`, the discovery pipeline, its listing and its `-ge 10` sanity check byte-for-byte; replace the bash size-balancing loop and its listing with `case "$SHARD" in 1|2|3) ;; *) echo "shard must be 1, 2 or 3" >&2; exit 1 ;; esac` and then exactly this command (keep the `timeout` wrapper as now):
     timeout --signal=INT --kill-after=60s 45m \
       apps/api/.venv/bin/python -m pytest "${fixture_backed[@]}" -q -p no:warnings -rs --durations=25 \
         -p finder_derived_data_shards --finder-shard "$SHARD" --finder-shards 3 \
         --finder-weights scripts/ci/finder_derived_data_weights.json \
         --finder-durations-out "$RUNNER_TEMP/finder-derived-data-durations-$SHARD.json"
   - add a final step `Upload shard durations` with `if: always()`, `uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1` (the repository's existing pin, copied exactly), `name: finder-derived-data-durations-${{ matrix.shard }}`, `path: ${{ runner.temp }}/finder-derived-data-durations-${{ matrix.shard }}.json`, `retention-days: 14`, `if-no-files-found: ignore`.
   - rewrite the job's comment block: three shards balanced by measured seconds (the numbers above), the dominant module split at test level by the plugin, and the refresh path (download the three durations artifacts of a green run, run the refresh tool, commit the new weights file).

   - real-data plan: collect the discovered modules ONCE with `sys.executable -m pytest --collect-only -q -p no:cacheprovider <modules>` (cwd = repository root, inherited environment; this needs no database and takes about 5 s), parse the node ids (lines containing "::"), call plan(nodeids, load_weights(<weights file>), 3, <file size>) and assert: every collected node id is assigned exactly once, max(totals) <= 1.3 * min(totals), and every split module has tests in all three shards. Load the plugin module with importlib from its file path;
   - the weights file passes load_weights and is byte-identical to json.dumps(data, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + "\n". Do NOT fail because a weighted module no longer exists or a discovered module is unweighted: other pull requests add and rename fixture-backed modules all the time (the fallback rate covers them until the next refresh).
